overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the notice-detail complaint was untimely and declined, and the late-approved minutes did not violate the law; a later reconsideration request was denied.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the February 13 meeting gave insufficient detail on a calendar topic (religious holidays). Declined as untimely, filed about two months after the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: When an alleged violation occurs in open session, the alleged violation can reasonably be discovered at the time it occurs.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to approve its February 13 minutes until after its March 5 meeting, contrary to the timely-approval requirement.
allegations.key_passage: We find that, despite the Committee's deviation from its general practice of approving minutes at its next meeting, its approval of the minutes at the following meeting, on April 9, did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Later raised (in the October reconsideration request) claims about a calendar motion and removal of religious holidays as discriminatory. Outside the Open Meeting Law, so not reviewed.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government's review concerns only compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
